analysis:
Both units are base_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (base lines 1021-1443), which is documentation only. The patch excerpt shows head changes only in the top release section (head lines 11-100): a v0.10.1 candidate header, upgrade/rollout notes, a libs/mlx-swift-lm pin bump, and a note that page-cache accounting is looser. I saw neither the rest of the head text nor the patch beyond its truncated excerpt.

No executable code, config, wire contract or authorization logic changes in what I saw, so I found no concrete security regression. Relevant retained controls are unchanged because only prose is in view: T-041/SEC-035 (30-minute SSD cache TTL, HMAC-keyed names, coordinator-authored cache scope), TB-011 App Attest authorization, and TB-002 coordinator-to-provider contract.

The visible patch text mentions several behavior changes. Nothing in the supplied evidence lets me verify any of them:
- Page-cache accounting counts more memory as available for load admission, KV budgets and cold-load capacity. This is a possible availability or memory-pressure concern, but the actual code is not supplied.
- The mlx-swift-lm pin moves from 7bed8216 to 6148b6da, which touches Swift sources only.
- GLM logprobs are deferred and the groundwork is disabled. The note says a 0.10.0 provider fails a logprob request with 500 generation_failure, which cools every provider of that model. That is a coordinator-dependency/availability rollout note, not a code defect in the supplied evidence.

The changelog entries from base lines 1021-1443 are historical text, and several describe security-relevant behavior: frozen legacy MDM cohort, App Attest requirements, cache routing persistence, and the SSD TTL raised to 30 minutes with SEC-035 re-acceptance. These are not changed by this PR in the visible patch. The full head text was not supplied, so the doc-only conclusion is limited to the visible excerpt. The next pass should check the actual code PRs behind the page-cache accounting change and the pin bump, since this unit gives no code evidence.
